title: Isandro and the Drop
premise: Silas Reyes, a disgraced intelligence analyst living off-grid in a government safe house, discovers the property has been listed online with interior photos — including shots of his hidden documents. The listing is bait set by Mara Voss, a former colleague turned private broker, who wants the one file Silas kept from his last agency job: proof that Deputy Director Alan Creel orchestrated a cover-up that killed three informants. As Silas races to verify the file before Voss's buyers destroy it, he realizes his only path to justice runs through exposing himself to the very system that erased him. In the end, Silas trades the original file for Voss's evidence chain against Creel, burns his own legend, and testifies under a new identity — choosing truth over the invisibility that once kept him alive.
about_author: Hazel Okonkwo is a former investigative journalist who spent six years covering corruption trials in West Africa and Eastern Europe before turning to fiction. She writes thrillers about people the systems they served would prefer forgotten.

chapters.title: The Listing
chapters.summary: Silas Reyes, scrolling real estate sites out of boredom, finds his safe house listed with photos of rooms only he has entered. POV: Silas. The emotional beat is cold dread — the careful architecture of his invisibility collapsing in a single browser tab. He notices one photo shows the edge of a document case he buried behind drywall.

chapters.title: Three Agencies, No Name
chapters.summary: Flashback interleave: Silas reconstructs how he was burned by three agencies, ending with the informant deaths he documented but could never prove. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: bitter self-examination as he decides whether the listing is a mistake or a message. He concludes someone wants him to see it — and that means they know exactly who he is.

chapters.title: Mara
chapters.summary: Voss contacts Silas directly through a dead-drop protocol only insiders know, offering to buy 'the contents of the house.' POV alternates between Silas surveilling the meet and Voss's calculated performance. Emotional beat: wary recognition between two people who once trusted each other. Silas realizes she isn't working alone — someone with agency access is her buyer.

chapters.title: What the Drywall Keeps
chapters.summary: Silas retrieves the file: raw intercepts implicating Deputy Director Creel in selling informant locations. POV: Silas, with tense second-person intrusions into his paranoia. Emotional beat: the weight of holding something worth killing for. He tests the file's authenticity and finds it genuine — but incomplete without Voss's corroborating chain of custody.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Shadow
chapters.summary: Silas tails Voss and identifies her buyer's fixer: a man he recognizes from Creel's old security detail. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: rising dread hardening into resolve. He understands the sale is a trap to confirm the file exists before it's seized and destroyed. He photographs the fixer and sends it to one journalist who owes him.

chapters.title: House of Mirrors
chapters.summary: The safe house is raided while Silas watches from across the street; the raiders plant nothing but take everything, including decoys he left. POV shifts briefly to the fixer reporting to an unseen voice. Emotional beat: humiliation transmuting into clarity — they wanted him to feel hunted so he'd run to Voss. Instead, Silas goes dark and plans his own sale.

chapters.title: Terms
chapters.summary: Silas counter-offers: the file for Voss's evidence chain and her client's name. Their negotiation in a shuttered aquarium becomes a duel of loyalties — she claims she's protecting whistleblowers, he accuses her of laundering power. POV: dual. Emotional beat: grudging respect. They agree on a simultaneous exchange, each certain the other will betray it.

chapters.title: Creel's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: POV: Creel, learning the file has surfaced, weighing whether killing Silas costs more than silence. Flashbacks reveal his genuine belief that sacrificed informants bought stability. Emotional beat: chilling self-justification. Creel orders the exchange site compromised, planning to bury file, broker, and analyst in one operation — and quietly arranges his own exit.

chapters.title: The Drop
chapters.summary: The exchange at a freight terminal collapses into violence when Creel's team breaches early. Voss takes a bullet shielding the evidence chain; Silas escapes with both halves of the proof after a brutal close-quarters fight. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: grief and fury fused into purpose. Dying Voss tells him where her insurance copy lives — and asks him to finish it.

chapters.title: On the Record
chapters.summary: Silas delivers the complete dossier to the journalist and an oversight committee, surrendering his anonymity to testify. Creel is indicted; Silas accepts witness protection not as erasure but as a new ledger. POV: Silas, closing with him signing his real name for the first time in years. Emotional beat: quiet vindication — loyalty to truth finally outweighing the safety of lies.
